sapience_notes.content: BimodalLogic is a DEPLOY-ONLY repository for the agent system: there is no local agent-system/ directory, and .claude-extensions.json resolves every extension source_dir to ~/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/*. Consequence measured here: .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh exits 1 with 11 FAILING suites (test-deploy-baseline-lib, test-gate-out-derived-staleness, test-gate-out-self-attribution, test-generate-task-order, test-lint-hook-registration-paths, test-manifest-scripts-sync, test-orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate, test-reconcile-demote-stranded, test-reconcile-handoff-status, test-resume-scan-nonconformance, test-sweep-invalidated-claims), every one asserting 'required source file(s) not found: .../agent-system/extensions/core/...'. They fail unconditionally in this repo regardless of the task and reference no Lean or typst path. Any dispatch here should attribute them under Condition 4 rather than re-triaging; the durable fix is for those suites to SKIP when the resolved source_dir is outside the repository.

A Lean MetaM/TacticM helper can be broken on every call while the whole project builds clean, because a MetaM failure is a RUNTIME failure of the elaborator, never a compile error. Measured instance: FormalSystem/Tactic/Meta.lean's buildContextExpr calls mkAppM ``List.nil`` with an explicit argument for List.nil's implicit type parameter, so it raises 'too many explicit arguments provided to @List.nil' on every input including the empty list, hard-failing modal_search on any box-headed goal -- and it compiled clean indefinitely. The 'it builds, so it works' heuristic does not extend to metaprogramming code: such code needs an executed #eval probe to be covered at all. Two pre-validated repairs: mkAppOptM ``List.nil`` #[some formulaType], or Lean.mkApp (Lean.mkConst ``List.nil`` [Level.zero]) formulaType.

In BimodalLogic, scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix moves a THIRD field beyond the two tests-* counts on any Tests/-only change: stamp-commit, which scripts/typst-status-counts.sh derives from git rev-parse --short HEAD. Under concurrent dispatches HEAD advances mid-task, so stamp-commit drifts for reasons unrelated to the edit. A plan's 'any field other than the tests-* counts moving means another writer's FormalSystem/ edit -- stop and diagnose' rule must exempt stamp-commit explicitly, or it produces a false alarm on every concurrent run. The genuine FormalSystem-drift signal is formalsystem-file-count / formalsystem-line-count.

Sizing a Lean test module from the number of FILES it must reach underestimates badly when the instruction is 'a #check per public declaration'. Measured: a ForMathlib smoke module planned at ~70 lines for five files came out at 141, almost entirely because FormalSystem/ForMathlib/Order/PFilter.lean alone declares 31 public declarations. Count the target files' public declarations, not their file count.

In BimodalLogic a new test module under Tests/ carries three non-obvious gate obligations, each discovered only by reading the gate scripts: (1) C6 requires the module be imported in Tests/BimodalTest.lean, since scripts/module-invariants-manifest.txt is empty and an unimported live module is an unreachable-module FAILURE; (2) a module with no row in scripts/c16-roots-baseline.txt has a docBlame ceiling of ZERO, so every new public declaration needs a docstring or `private`; (3) the warning budget is zero under CI's --wfail, with a measured exemption only for /-- info: ... -/ expected-output lines (104-133 chars observed) and not for code lines. All three held exactly as predicted across two new modules in this task.

FormalSystem/Semantics/Nomic/Witnesses.lean's F3 does NOT synthesize an F3.IsRegular instance: F3 is a plain def, so the instance head is not syntactically `ofStepFamily ...` until F3 unfolds. Any use of a regularity-requiring nomic theorem at F3 must bind it as a bare term, `haveI : F3.IsRegular := NomicFrame.ofStepFamily_isRegular R3 R3.fwd R3.bwd`, exactly as NomicLanguage/NomicFour.lean does. This is a general Lean pattern worth remembering: a concrete witness defined by `def` rather than `abbrev` silently loses instance resolution through its definitional unfolding.
